editorial.headline: Sharia Bullion Banking: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This sharia-based bullion banking activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the province-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
**A foreign investor cannot register this activity at a Bali address today.** Nationally, the activity is open to PMA and carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, however, the recorded outcome is a block under the province-wide PMA moratorium. That contrast is not a minor qualification to an otherwise open classification; it is the decisive fact for an operator considering where to place the registration.

At its centre, this is sharia bullion banking. The activity primarily accepts deposits of precious metals, including gold or silver, held as bars or currency, and channels loans of those precious metals. The same asset sits on both sides of the banking activity: bullion is deposited and bullion is lent. Everything is conducted according to sharia principles, which the scope places within the definition of the activity itself. This is therefore a precise banking classification rooted in precious-metal deposits and lending, rather than a broad label for any business associated with gold or silver.

At national level, the slim record makes the activity available at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. It does not confine registration to a single size of enterprise. For a PMA registration nationally, the status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign stake is 100%, allowing full foreign ownership within the national position recorded here. The stated national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Those facts establish the national frame clearly: an open PMA status, a full foreign-ownership ceiling, and availability across the four named scales.

Bali requires a different conclusion. Its status is recorded as Closed (Bali moratorium), and the activity is explicitly blocked for PMA. The stated reason is that the Besar scale is classified as Low risk, bringing it within Bali’s PMA moratorium. That moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA throughout the province, on a permanent and island-wide basis. The cited governor’s letter is from May 2026, with the record also noting June 2026. For a Bali address, the moratorium—not national openness—decides the result.
